title: fix: guard against NaN/float in gas oracle BigInt conversion
description:
> Oracle guards now catch the NaN,
> Math.round tames the float,
> gas price errors handled with grace,
> no more BigInt bloat.

## What it solves

The gas oracle parsing in `useDefaultGasPrice` crashes with "The number NaN cannot be converted to a BigInt" when oracle responses contain undefined/invalid values, or when floating-point multiplication produces non-integer results before `BigInt()` conversion. This causes repeated console errors every 20 seconds during gas price polling.

Related: [WA-1920](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-1920/twap-order-flow-glitches-on-web-with-pending-signer) — this fix addresses the NaN console errors observed during investigation, but does not resolve the UI flickering issue itself.

## How this PR fixes it

Adds `Number.isFinite()` validation before `BigInt()` conversion and `Math.round()` to handle floating-point precision in both Etherscan and non-Etherscan oracle parsing paths. Invalid values now throw descriptive errors that flow through the existing oracle fallback chain (try next oracle → try fixed config → surface error to hook consumer) instead of crashing with an opaque TypeError.

Also adds a comprehensive test suite for `useDefaultGasPrice` (27 tests) since none existed previously.

## How to test it

1. Run the new tests: `cd packages/utils && npx jest --testPathPattern='useDefaultGasPrice' --no-watchman`
2. Run the existing web gas price tests: `cd apps/web && npx jest --testPathPattern='useGasPrice' --no-watchman`
3. Verify gas fee estimation works on the transaction confirmation screen (any chain)

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Oracle response] --> B{Valid number?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Math.round + BigInt]
    B -->|No / NaN / Infinity| D[Throw descriptive error]
    D --> E[Caught by fallback loop]
    E --> F[Try next oracle or fixed config]
```

findings.claim: Much of this new test suite duplicates cases already covered in apps/web/src/hooks/__tests__/useGasPrice.test.ts (first oracle, fallback to second oracle, fixed fallback, fixed 1559, speed-up), creating redundant test coverage across the two files.
The tests replace global.fetch with a jest mock instead of using MSW, which deviates from the project's stated rule (AGENTS.md:374) to use MSW rather than mocking fetch directly.
This is a second repetition of the same multiply/check/round/convert logic noted at lines 55-65, reinforcing the duplication issue.

Test data (makeChain and the fee-data helper) is built using type casts (as unknown as Chain, as unknown as FeeData) instead of the existing faker-based chainBuilder in packages/utils/src/tests/builders/chains.ts, which conflicts with the project's guidance to use faker-based builders and properly typed helpers rather than type casts.

The guard conflates an unknown/invalid value with a real zero value; values should be parsed with a helper that explicitly rejects null, empty or whitespace strings, non-finite numbers, and zero or negative results, with corresponding tests added for each case.

The Etherscan parsing path has the same issue as the non-Etherscan path: null values in the response would be coerced to 0 by Number(null) and pass validation instead of being treated as missing data.
Because no test produces a fractional wei value, removing Math.round here would not cause any test to fail, leaving the new rounding behavior unprotected by tests.
The same finite-number-only guard applied to the Etherscan maxFeePerGas calculation lets an empty FastGasPrice value pass through as zero instead of being rejected.

The sequence of multiplying by gweiFactor, checking finiteness, rounding, and converting to BigInt is repeated three times in the file instead of being extracted into a shared helper, making it easy for a future fix (such as the positivity check) to be applied in only some of the places.

The finite-number guard does not reject null or empty/whitespace string values, since Number(''), Number('  '), and Number(null) all evaluate to 0 and pass the check; an oracle returning an empty or null value therefore produces a zero gas price instead of triggering a fallback to the next oracle.
Negative values are not rejected by the guard, so a negative oracle value would also pass through as a valid (negative) gas price.
The provider test double is cast with as never instead of being properly typed, which is another instance of using type casts in place of proper builders/typing.
The getTotalFee 'large values' test case is identical to the one in apps/web/src/hooks/__tests__/useGasPrice.test.ts:334-337, duplicating test logic instead of consolidating it.
The same missing positivity check exists at this second location, allowing zero, empty, null, or negative oracle values to be accepted as a valid gas price.

When data[gasParameter] is null, Number(null) evaluates to 0, which passes the Number.isFinite() check even though it is not a valid oracle value; the code should explicitly check for null and throw a missing-parameter error instead of silently treating it as zero.

The new parsing/validation logic lives in unexported pure functions (parseEtherscanOracleResult and the conversion step in fetchGasOracle), so every edge case must be exercised indirectly through renderHook, a mocked fetch, and waitFor rather than being tested directly.

The test inputs '22.846685108', '20.123456789' and 25.5, when multiplied by 1e9, all produce exact integers, so BigInt() accepts them without needing Math.round; these tests do not actually exercise the fractional-value fix.

This second floating-point test has the same problem: its expected values are computed using the identical BigInt(Math.round(x * 1e9)) formula used in the implementation, so it cannot detect a disagreement, and an input like '1.1' (which yields a non-integer product) with a literal expected value should be used instead.

This floating-point test uses input values (22.846685108 * 1e9, 20.123456789 * 1e9, 25.5 * 1e9) that all evaluate to exact integers, so the test would still pass even if the Math.round fix were removed from the implementation.

The conversion step in fetchGasOracle should be extracted into a pure, exported function such as parseOracleResponse(json, gasParameter, gweiFactor) and tested directly with a table of inputs and outputs, keeping only a few hook-level tests for fallback and error handling.
A gweiFactor value of an empty string coerces to 0, which would silently turn every computed result into 0n rather than causing a validation failure.

Number(''), Number(' ') and Number(null) all evaluate to 0, which passes the Number.isFinite check, and negative numeric strings also pass; this lets an oracle response with an empty, null, or negative gas price value be treated as a valid, winning price instead of being rejected so the code falls through to the next oracle or fixed config.
This second float test case has the same problem as the one at line 241: its inputs yield exact integer wei values, so it passes even without Math.round and does not verify the fix.
Same as the line 64/65 issue: this second Math.round call is also not covered by a test that would fail if the rounding were removed.
